tests.title: A patch is added and its branch resolved by the documented order
given: a carry_patch workspace with a branch in its own repository, one present only as the fork's fetched copy, and one only on the fork
tests.when: each is added, with patch_branch_source hub and then origin, and once with skip_branch_check
then: each add answers 201 with status active and a position
the resolutions are local, origin_tracking and origin_fetch respectively
origin_fetch happens only with patch_branch_source origin
skip_branch_check reports skipped and creates no branch
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' integration test file, table over (branchLocation, setting, expectedResolution)

tests.title: A position inserts and shifts, and past the end appends
given: a workspace with three patches
tests.when: patches are added at position 1, at position 3, at position 99 and with no position
then: each insert moves the patches at and after it down by one
a position past the end and an omitted position both append
the positions are 1 to n with no gap after each add
tests.pseudocode: in the patch list test file, table over the positions asserting the resulting order

tests.title: if_not_exists answers with the existing patch
given: a workspace whose list already holds a branch
tests.when: the same branch is added with if_not_exists and then without it
then: the first answers 200 with the existing patch unchanged
the second answers 409
no second patch is added in either case
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' test file: assert post(branch, if_not_exists=True).status == 200 and post(branch).status == 409

tests.title: A batch validates all syntax first and then all branches
given: a carry_patch workspace and a fork
tests.when: a batch is sent whose first element names a missing branch and whose second has position 0, and then a batch whose second element names a missing branch after a first whose branch must be created
then: the first batch answers for the second element's syntax, not the first element's missing branch
the second batch is refused whole and adds no patch
the branch created for its first element remains and resolves as local on a later add
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' integration test file: assert 'patch[1]' in post(batchA).json.error.message; post(batchB); assert patches() == [] and resolution(retry) == 'local'

tests.title: Malformed adds are refused and change nothing
given: a carry_patch workspace, a standard one and an archived one
tests.when: adds are made with no branch name, an empty one, the integration branch, position 0, a branch that cannot be resolved, and against the standard and archived workspaces
then: each answers 400
a batch element's message begins with patch[i]
the patch list is unchanged in every case
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' test file, table over the refused adds asserting 400 and an unchanged list

tests.title: Duplicates, a busy workspace and a failed fork fetch are refused
given: a workspace whose list holds a branch, a workspace whose lock is held, and a fork that refuses a fetch
tests.when: the existing branch is added, a batch names one branch twice, a branch needing creation is added while the lock is held, and a branch is added that needs a fork fetch that fails
then: the duplicate and the repeated batch entry answer 409
the busy workspace answers 409 workspace_busy
the failed fetch answers 502 with error_type origin_fetch_failed
the list is unchanged in every case
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' test file, table over the four cases asserting status, error_type and an unchanged list

tests.title: Patches are listed in position order without deleted ones
given: a carry_patch workspace with four patches of which one is deleted, and a standard workspace
tests.when: each workspace's patches are listed
then: the carry_patch workspace returns three patches in ascending position order
the deleted patch is absent
the standard workspace returns an empty array
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' test file: assert [p.position for p in list()] == [1,2,3] and deleted.id not in ids(list())

tests.title: One patch is read, a deleted one included, with its replaced tip where one is kept
given: a live patch with a kept replaced tip, a live patch with none, a deleted patch, and a workspace with no repository
tests.when: each is read
then: each answers 200 with the patch
replaced_sha is the 40-character SHA only where a backup exists
it is absent for the workspace with no repository, and a failed lookup does not fail the request
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' integration test file, table over the four cases asserting the presence of replaced_sha

tests.title: An update changes the fields it names and keeps the list contiguous
given: a workspace with four patches
tests.when: a patch's position, status, description and upstream pull request are changed, singly and together, and a branch_name is included in a body
then: each named field changes and the others do not
the branch_name in the body is ignored
the positions are 1 to n after a position change
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' test file, table over the fields asserting the change and the resulting positions

tests.title: Invalid updates are refused
given: a workspace with two patches and one deleted patch
tests.when: updates set an unknown status, the status deleted, a position of 0 and of n+1, name a patch that does not exist, and target the deleted patch
then: the invalid status, the status deleted and the out-of-range positions answer 400
the unknown patch answers 404
the deleted patch answers 409
no patch changes
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' test file, table over the six cases asserting status and an unchanged patch

tests.title: Positions stay contiguous under any sequence of operations
given: a carry_patch workspace and the patch operations: add, update position, remove, restore, reorder and rebuild
tests.when: generated sequences of those operations are applied
then: after every operation the non-deleted patches hold positions 1 to n
no position is repeated and none is skipped
tests.pseudocode: in the patch list test file, a generative test over operation sequences asserting positions == list(range(1, n+1))

tests.title: Removing a patch closes the positions and discards its backup
given: a workspace with three patches, the middle one holding a kept replaced tip
tests.when: the middle patch is removed, and a removal is made where discarding the backup fails
then: each answers 204
the remaining patches hold positions 1 and 2
the backup is gone after the first
the failed discard does not change the answer
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' integration test file: delete(mid); assert [p.position for p in list()] == [1,2] and backup(mid) is None

tests.title: A deleted patch is restored to the end as active
given: a workspace with two live patches and one deleted
tests.when: the deleted patch is restored
then: the response is 200 with status active
its position is the last
deleted_at is null
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' test file: r = post(restore); assert r.json.status == 'active' and r.json.position == 3 and r.json.deleted_at is None

tests.title: A reorder sets the whole list's order
given: a workspace with three patches
tests.when: the reorder route is called with their ids in a new order
then: the response is 200 with every patch in the new order
the first id holds position 1 and the last position 3
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' test file: r = post(reorder, [c, a, b]); assert [p.id for p in r.json] == [c, a, b]

tests.title: Bad reorders and restores are refused
given: a workspace with three patches, a live patch, and another workspace's patch
tests.when: reorders are sent that are empty, omit an id, repeat one and name a foreign patch, and restores are called on a live patch, on a standard workspace and on an archived one
then: each reorder answers 400 and no position changes
the restore of a live patch answers 400
an unknown patch answers 404
tests.pseudocode: in the patch routes' test file, two tables asserting the status and an unchanged list

tests.title: reset-to-origin checks its preconditions in order
given: an archived workspace, a standard one, one that is not ready, a missing patch, the integration branch and a merged_upstream patch
tests.when: reset-to-origin is called for each, including combinations where two preconditions would both fail
then: the answer is the one belonging to the earlier check in each combination

an archived or standard workspace answers 400, a workspace that is not ready answers 409, a missing patch answers 404, the integration branch answers 400 and a merged_upstream or deleted patch answers 409
tests.pseudocode: in the reset-to-origin test file, table over (conditions, expectedStatus)

tests.title: reset-to-origin applies the first rule that fits
given: a patch the workspace lacks, one at the same commit as the fork, one the fork has advanced beyond, and one that has diverged
tests.when: reset-to-origin is called for each
then: the actions reported are created, none, fast_forwarded and replaced respectively
the branch is at the fork's tip afterwards in every case but none
the none case writes nothing and still answers 200
tests.pseudocode: in the reset-to-origin integration test file, table over the four cases asserting the action and the resulting ref

tests.title: A reset that discards commits keeps the old tip
given: a patch branch that has diverged from the fork, and one that already has an earlier backup
tests.when: reset-to-origin is called for each
then: the old tip is recoverable afterwards and is reported as replaced_sha
the earlier backup is superseded by the new one
a fast-forward keeps no backup
tests.pseudocode: in the reset-to-origin integration test file: r = post(reset); assert r.json.replaced_sha == oldTip and backup(branch) == oldTip

tests.title: A reset that moves an active patch queues a rebuild
given: an active patch, a conflict patch, a disabled patch, a workspace with auto_rebuild_after_sync false, and one with a rebuild already queued
tests.when: reset-to-origin moves the branch in each case
then: the active and conflict patches queue a rebuild and report its id
the disabled patch queues none
auto_rebuild_after_sync false queues none
an existing queued rebuild is not duplicated and rebuild_triggered is false
tests.pseudocode: in the reset-to-origin integration test file, table over the five cases asserting rebuild_triggered and the job count

tests.title: reset-to-origin reports its failures without leaving the patch inconsistent
given: a fork without the branch, a branch another operation changes mid-reset, a fork that cannot be fetched, a held lock, and a store that fails the read-back after the move
tests.when: reset-to-origin is called in each case
then: the statuses are 409 missing_on_origin, 409 ref_changed, 502 origin_fetch_failed, 409 workspace_busy and 500 respectively
the patch record is never left describing a move that did not happen
tests.pseudocode: in the reset-to-origin integration test file, table over the five failures asserting status, error_type and the patch record

tests.title: A carry-patch sync fetches the upstream, and the fork only when configured to
given: a carry_patch workspace with patch_branch_source hub, and one with origin, each with a recording upstream and fork
tests.when: each is synced
then: both fetch the upstream
the hub-sourced workspace makes no request to the fork and reports origin_fetched false
the origin-sourced workspace fetches the fork, pruning branches it deleted, and reports origin_fetched true
tests.pseudocode: in the carry-patch sync integration test file, table over the setting asserting fork.requests and origin_fetched

tests.title: The sync's steps run in the documented order
given: failures injected at the credential resolution, the upstream fetch and the fork fetch in turn
tests.when: a sync is run against each
then: a failure at an earlier step prevents the later ones
the credential failure answers 502 and fetches nothing
the upstream fetch failure answers 502 and never fetches the fork
the fork fetch failure answers 502 with origin_fetch_failed after the upstream was fetched
tests.pseudocode: in the carry-patch sync integration test file, table over the injected failures asserting the status and which fetches happened

tests.title: An upstream force-push is reported, not refused
given: a carry_patch workspace whose upstream history was rewritten since the last sync
tests.when: the sync runs
then: the response is 200 with force_push_detected true
upstream_head_sha advances to the rewritten head
the queued rebuild applies the patches to the rewritten upstream
tests.pseudocode: in the carry-patch sync integration test file: r = post(sync); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.force_push_detected is True

tests.title: Patch branches are refreshed from the fork under the divergence policy
given: patches whose branches are missing on the fork, absent locally, identical, behind the fork and diverged
the replace and the report policies
the integration branch and a merged_upstream patch
tests.when: a sync runs with patch_branch_source origin under each policy, and once with patch_branch_source hub
then: the actions are missing_on_origin, created, none, fast_forwarded and, under replace, replaced with the old tip kept, or under report, diverged and left alone
patches_diverged is empty under replace and lists the branch under report
the integration branch is never refreshed and a merged_upstream patch is not refreshed
each patch's origin state, SHA and time are recorded, and with patch_branch_source hub all three are cleared
tests.pseudocode: in the carry-patch sync integration test file, table over (branchState, policy) asserting the action, the resulting ref and the recorded origin fields

tests.title: Patches merged upstream are found by the configured strategies
given: a patch contained in the upstream by ancestry, one whose commits the upstream has by content, one whose pull request number appears in a recent upstream commit message, and one that is in none of those
tests.when: a sync runs under squash_merge_detection ancestry_only, content_based and both
then: ancestry_only matches the ancestry case alone
content_based matches the content and pull request cases
both matches all three
each matched patch becomes merged_upstream, has its origin fields cleared and is listed in patches_merged
the unrelated patch is never matched
tests.pseudocode: in the carry-patch sync integration test file, table over (strategy, patchKind, expectedMatch)

tests.title: A sync queues one rebuild under the documented conditions
given: syncs where the upstream advanced, where only a disabled patch's branch moved, where an active patch's branch moved, where a patch became merged upstream, and where nothing changed
workspaces with auto_rebuild_after_sync false and with a rebuild already queued
tests.when: each sync runs
then: a rebuild is queued when the upstream advanced, an active or conflict patch's branch moved, or a patch became merged upstream
none is queued when nothing changed, when only a disabled patch's branch moved, or when auto_rebuild_after_sync is false
an existing queued or running rebuild is not duplicated, and rebuild_triggered is false with rebuild_job_id absent rather than null
tests.pseudocode: in the carry-patch sync integration test file, table over the conditions asserting rebuild_triggered and the queued job count

tests.title: A failed branch refresh ends the sync with its partial effects recorded
given: syncs where writing a branch fails, where the ancestry comparison fails, and where the working state cannot follow a moved branch
tests.when: each sync runs after one branch has already been moved
then: each answers 500 with a message distinguishing the three cases
the outcomes already reached are recorded on their patches
a rebuild is queued for the branch already moved, unless auto_rebuild_after_sync is false
neither upstream_head_sha nor last_sync_at is written
tests.pseudocode: in the carry-patch sync integration test file, table over the three failures asserting the message, the recorded outcomes and the unwritten sync fields

tests.title: A completed carry-patch sync answers with its own fields
given: a carry_patch workspace with patch_branch_source hub and one with origin
tests.when: each is synced, once where nothing advanced
then: each answers 200 with every workspace field plus patches_merged, rebuild_triggered, force_push_detected and origin_fetched
patches_synced and patches_diverged appear only with patch_branch_source origin
sync_error is not set on this path
last_sync_at is updated even when nothing advanced
tests.pseudocode: in the carry-patch sync integration test file: r = post(sync); assert set(EXTRA_FIELDS) <= set(r.json) and r.json.sync_error is None

tests.title: A rebuild starts from the fetched upstream head and applies patches in order
given: a carry_patch workspace with four active patches and an upstream that advances between the submit and the start
tests.when: a rebuild runs
then: the job records the upstream head it fetched at its start
the patches are attempted in ascending position order
the results are reported in that order
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild integration test file: j = run_rebuild(); assert j.upstream_head_sha == fetched and [r.position for r in j.patch_results] == [1,2,3,4]

tests.title: A rebuild skips the patches it must, with reasons
given: a stack holding a merged_upstream patch, a disabled one, a deleted one, one whose branch is missing and two ordinary ones
tests.when: a rebuild runs
then: each of the four is reported skipped with the reason merged_upstream, disabled, deleted or branch_not_found
none of them contributes to the result
the two ordinary patches are applied
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild test file: j = run_rebuild(); assert {r.branch_name: r.skipped_reason for r in j.patch_results if r.status == 'skipped'} == expected

tests.title: A conflict ends or is carried past according to the fail mode
given: a stack of three patches whose second conflicts, with no recorded resolution and then with one
tests.when: a rebuild runs with fail_fast and with continue, in each case
then: with fail_fast and no resolution the job fails, reporting the conflicting patch and its files
with continue and no resolution the patch is marked conflict, its changes are left out and the third patch is still attempted
with a recorded resolution the patch applies cleanly under both fail modes
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild integration test file, table over (failMode, resolutionRecorded) asserting the job status and the patch statuses

tests.title: A rebuild's end sets the branch, retires merged patches and closes the positions
given: a stack with one merged_upstream patch among four
tests.when: a rebuild completes
then: the integration branch is at the rebuilt head
the merged patch has status deleted with deleted_at set
the remaining patches hold positions 1 to 3
the job reports both the new and the previous integration head
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild integration test file: j = run_rebuild(); assert ref(integration) == j.integration_head_sha and positions() == [1,2,3]

tests.title: The integration branch is pushed to the fork when the setting says so, and a failure does not fail the job
given: a workspace with rebuild_push_integration_branch true against a fork that accepts, one against a fork that refuses, and one with the setting false
tests.when: a rebuild completes in each
then: the accepting case force-pushes the branch and reports integration_branch_pushed true
the refusing case still completes the job
the setting false pushes nothing
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild integration test file, table over the three cases asserting the job status and the fork's refs

tests.title: A tip that moves mid-rebuild yields one follow-up job
given: a rebuild in progress and a patch tip that is advanced while it applies patches, and separately an upstream head that advances
tests.when: each rebuild completes
then: the completed job's result reflects the tips it started with
exactly one follow-up rebuild is queued
the follow-up is recorded as submitted by the system rather than a user
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild integration test file: start(); move_tip(); wait(); assert queued_rebuilds() == 1 and followup.submitted_by.startswith('system')

tests.title: A rebuild holds the lock only at its start and its end
given: a rebuild made to spend measurable time applying patches
tests.when: a sync, a merge submit, a rerere forget, a rollback, a branch push, an archive and a reclone are each attempted while it applies patches
then: the sync, merge, rerere forget, rollback and branch push all succeed
the archive and the reclone answer 409 workspace_busy
an operation attempted during the rebuild's start or end window answers 409 workspace_busy
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild integration test file, table over the operations asserting success or workspace_busy during the applying phase

tests.title: A running rebuild's per-patch results grow as it proceeds
given: a rebuild over four patches, made to pause between them
tests.when: the job is read after each patch finishes
then: each read returns the results of the patches completed so far
the number of results grows monotonically
the job's status reads running until it completes
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild integration test file: counts = [len(read(job).patch_results) for _ in range(4)]; assert counts == sorted(counts) and counts[-1] == 4

tests.title: A rebuild is submitted and queued with the right strategy and fail mode
given: a ready carry_patch workspace with active patches and settings naming a strategy and a fail mode
tests.when: a rebuild is submitted with no body, with a strategy, and with both a strategy and a fail mode
then: each answers 202 with the queued job carrying its id, type, status queued and payload
the body's values override the settings and an absent body uses the settings
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild routes' integration test file, table over the bodies asserting 202 and the effective strategy

tests.title: A rebuild submit is refused for every documented reason
given: a standard workspace, a carry_patch workspace that is not ready, one with no active or conflict patch, and one with a rebuild already queued
tests.when: a rebuild is submitted for each, and with an invalid strategy and an invalid fail mode
then: the standard workspace answers 400 workspace_mode_mismatch
no active patches answers 400 no_active_patches
the unready workspace and the invalid fields answer 400
the existing rebuild answers 409 concurrent_rebuild
no job is queued in any case
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild routes' test file, table over the six cases asserting status, error_type and the job count

tests.title: Rebuild jobs are listed and read
given: a workspace with three rebuild jobs and another workspace with one
tests.when: the jobs are listed, one is read, another workspace's job is read, and an unknown id is read
then: the list answers 200 newest first
the read answers 200 with the job and its per-patch results
the foreign job and the unknown id both answer 404
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild routes' test file: assert [j.id for j in list()] == newest_first; assert read(foreign).status == 404

tests.title: A queued rebuild is cancelled and a dead-lettered one requeued
given: jobs at queued, running, completed, failed, dead_letter and cancelled
tests.when: each is cancelled and each is requeued, and a dead-lettered job is requeued while another rebuild is queued
then: cancelling the queued job answers 200 with status cancelled and every other status answers 409
requeuing the dead-lettered job answers 200 with status queued and every other status answers 409
requeuing while another rebuild is queued answers 409
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild routes' test file, table over (jobStatus, action, expected)

tests.title: A completed rebuild is rolled back to the previous integration head
given: a workspace with two completed rebuilds, a first rebuild with no previous head, and one whose lock is held
tests.when: each is rolled back, and once against a store whose branch reset fails
then: the rollback answers 200 reporting the SHA it rolled back to and the integration branch is at it
the first rebuild answers 409
the held lock answers 409 workspace_busy
the failed reset answers 500 and leaves the branch where it was
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild routes' integration test file, table over the four cases asserting status and the integration branch

tests.title: The preview predicts every patch without writing anything
given: a stack holding patches that would apply, one that would conflict, a disabled one, a merged_upstream one and one whose branch is missing
tests.when: the preview is requested, and requested for a standard workspace
then: each attempted patch is reported would_succeed with a tree or would_conflict with its files
a predicted conflict does not stop the later predictions
the disabled and merged_upstream patches are not attempted
a patch whose branch is missing is reported would_succeed
no ref or object of the repository changes
the standard workspace answers 400
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild routes' integration test file: before = refs(); r = get(preview); assert refs() == before and statuses(r) == expected

tests.title: Recorded resolutions are listed with their state
given: a workspace with a resolution recorded while its path was known, one recorded by an earlier rebuild with no known path, a conflict seen but unresolved, and a workspace with none
tests.when: the resolutions are listed for each
then: the listing answers 200 newest first with id, path, recorded_at and resolved
path is null where it is not known
resolved is true only where a resolution will be replayed
the workspace with none answers an empty resolutions array
tests.pseudocode: in the rerere routes' integration test file: r = get(rerere); assert [e.resolved for e in r.json.resolutions] == expected

tests.title: A resolution is forgotten by identity or by a path in conflict
given: two recorded resolutions, one for a path currently in conflict
tests.when: one is forgotten by identity and the other by path, and a rebuild is then run that reaches each conflict
then: each forget answers 204 and the entry is gone from the listing
the next rebuild reports each conflict rather than replaying it
tests.pseudocode: in the rerere routes' integration test file: delete(rerere, id); assert id not in ids(list()); assert run_rebuild().conflicts

tests.title: A bad or unmatched forget is refused
given: a workspace with one recorded resolution and a held lock in one case
tests.when: forgets are called with an empty pathspec, a pathspec starting with a hyphen, an identity matching nothing, a path with no recorded resolution, and against the busy workspace
then: the empty and invalid pathspecs answer 400, checked before the workspace is looked up
the unmatched identity and path answer 404
the busy workspace answers 409 workspace_busy
nothing is removed in any case
tests.pseudocode: in the rerere routes' test file, table over the five cases asserting status and an unchanged listing

tests.title: The dashboard reports the workspace, the latest rebuild and every patch
given: a carry_patch workspace with patches at several statuses, one with a conflict in the latest rebuild, and one whose latest rebuild has not run
tests.when: the dashboard is requested
then: the response is 200 with the documented object
patches are in position order and deleted ones are absent
each patch carries its latest rebuild result or null, with conflicting files only where that result is a conflict
last_rebuild is the latest job's id and status, or null when none has run
tests.pseudocode: in the dashboard integration test file: r = get(patch_status); assert [p.position for p in r.json.patches] == sorted(...) and r.json.last_rebuild.status in STATUSES

tests.title: The dashboard's counts agree with the patches it lists
given: generated workspaces with patches across every status and origin state, under both patch_branch_source settings
tests.when: the dashboard is requested for each
then: total_patches equals the length of the patches array and the sum of the four status counts
patches_diverged and patches_missing_on_origin count the patches whose origin state says so, and are 0 with patch_branch_source hub
total_rerere_resolutions is 0 when the resolutions cannot be read
tests.pseudocode: in the dashboard test file, a generative test asserting the identities between summary and patches

tests.title: The dashboard refuses a standard workspace
given: a standard workspace
tests.when: the dashboard is requested
then: the response is 400 in the error envelope
tests.pseudocode: in the dashboard test file: assert get(patch_status, standardWs).status == 400

tests.title: An accepted push to a patch branch queues a rebuild without delaying the push
given: a carry_patch workspace with a registered patch branch, with auto_rebuild_after_push true and then false
tests.when: a push updating that branch is accepted, and a push updating an ordinary branch is accepted
then: with the setting true a rebuild is queued for the patch branch push
the push's answer does not wait for the rebuild
with the setting false none is queued
the ordinary branch queues none
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild trigger integration test file, table over (branchKind, setting) asserting the queued job count and the push's latency

tests.title: At most one rebuild is queued for a workspace whatever triggered it
given: a workspace with a rebuild already queued, and one with a rebuild running
tests.when: a push, a sync and a reset-to-origin each occur that would otherwise queue a rebuild
then: no second rebuild is queued in any case
the sync and the reset report rebuild_triggered false
once the first rebuild completes a later trigger queues one again
tests.pseudocode: in the rebuild trigger integration test file: assert queued_count() == 1 after each trigger

tests.title: A patch is registered and the stack rebuilt against a running deployment
given: a running deployment with a real carry_patch workspace, a real upstream and a branch pushed to Parley
tests.when: afc patch add is run, then afc rebuild submit --wait
then: the add exits 0 and prints the patch as active
the rebuild reaches completed and prints a result per patch
the integration branch is at the rebuilt head
tests.pseudocode: in the carry-patch smoke test file: run('afc patch add'); r = run('afc rebuild submit --wait'); assert r.exit == 0 and json(r.stdout).status == 'completed'

tests.title: An upstream advance is absorbed by a sync and its rebuild
given: a running deployment, a carry_patch workspace, and a real upstream that has taken one of the patches and advanced
tests.when: afc workspace sync --wait is run and the dashboard is then read
then: the sync reports the merged patch and a queued rebuild
the rebuild completes and the merged patch becomes deleted
the remaining positions are contiguous and the dashboard shows the new integration head
tests.pseudocode: in the carry-patch smoke test file: r = run('afc workspace sync --wait'); assert merged in json(r.stdout).patches_merged; assert run('afc workspace patch-status').exit == 0

tests.title: A conflict is recorded once and replayed on the next rebuild
given: a running deployment and a carry_patch workspace whose second patch conflicts with the upstream
tests.when: a rebuild is run with the continue fail mode, the conflict is resolved, and a second rebuild is run
then: the first rebuild completes with that patch marked conflict and its files reported
the second rebuild applies the patch cleanly with no conflict reported
afc rerere list shows the recorded resolution between the two
tests.pseudocode: in the carry-patch smoke test file: run('afc rebuild submit --fail-mode continue --wait'); resolve(); assert 'conflict' not in run('afc rebuild submit --wait').stdout

tests.title: A diverged patch branch is reported and then reset
given: a running deployment, a carry_patch workspace with patch_branch_source origin and patch_divergence_policy report, and a fork whose patch branch has diverged
tests.when: afc workspace sync is run, then afc patch reset-to-origin
then: the sync lists the branch in patches_diverged
the reset moves the branch to the fork's tip and prints the replaced SHA
a rebuild is queued and its id is printed
tests.pseudocode: in the carry-patch smoke test file: assert branch in json(run('afc workspace sync').stdout).patches_diverged; r = run('afc patch reset-to-origin'); assert json(r.stdout).replaced_sha
